QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_38

question.text: Section 5.11.4 describes three primary data collection methods: Observation, Interview, and FGD. Which statement correctly characterises the OBSERVATION method?

answer.text: It requires extensive interaction with respondents via structured questions

The information is collected via direct observation using an observation checklist without interacting with respondents; focused on what is currently happening; independent of respondent willingness to respond
It replaces FGDs as a superior qualitative method
It can be applied only to digital projects

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.11.4 defines Observation: 'The information is collected with direct observation using the observation checklist without interacting with the respondents. The information captured under this method is focused on what is currently happening; it is not impacted by either the past or future instances. This method is independent of respondent's willingness to respond.' The Trap: A describes the Interview method. C overstates observation's merits. D wrongly limits its domain. Cross-Exam Context: Research methodology courses reference the same observational framework; XXIII applies it to on-site NGO visits. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Pair observation with short informant interviews at the same site — the observed behaviour provides the baseline and the interview supplies the 'why', together producing richer evidence than either alone.
